title: A product over a pointwise product splits into two products
statement: The product over [0,n) of a pointwise product of two functions equals the product of the two functions' own products over [0,n). The successor step is the four-factor rearrangement (A*B)*(a*b) = (A*a)*(B*b).

formal.statement: theorem Nat.prodRange_mul : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.prodRange (fun (x3 : AxNat) => AxNat.mul (x0 x3) (x1 x3)) x2) (AxNat.mul (AxNat.prodRange x0 x2) (AxNat.prodRange x1 x2)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.prodRange_mul is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- prodRange_mul 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE '^Nat\.prodRange_mul.5.\(\(x0 : \(\(x0 : AxNat\) -> AxNat\)\) -> \(\(x1 : \(\(x1 : AxNat\) -> AxNat\)\) -> \(\(x2 : AxNat\) -> Eq\.\{1\} AxNat \(AxNat\.prodRange \(fun \(x3 : AxNat\) => AxNat\.mul \(x0 x3\) \(x1 x3\)\) x2\) \(AxNat\.mul \(AxNat\.prodRange x0 x2\) \(AxNat\.prodRange x1 x2\)\)\)\)\)$')" = 1

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by `nat_prelude/multiset_prod.rs` (lane nat-factorization).

notes: The Nat twin of `Int.prodRange_mul`. The statement's left-hand side is the LITERAL lambda `fun i => mul (f i) (g i)`, so a caller whose fold is written in any other beta-equivalent shape relies on the kernel's defeq to line the two up; that is what `Nat.Multiset.prod_add` does. It says nothing about a SUM over a pointwise product, and nothing about folds over different bounds.
